reviews.comment: Dr. Ayres gives obscure, bare-minimum responses to questions. This was the case in speaking to her in person as well as email. It was very frustrating. Her lab instructions are quite vague, both verbally and in the PowerPoints/protocols we were given. With every step, students had to ask for clarification. Dealing with this woman was exhausting.

Dr. Ayres is a great professor; shes present to oversee the lab and provide additional support to TAs. Quizzes and Exams are open note, write everything down. My class served as the guinea pigs for the new class setup, and it worked out fine. Follow basic lab rules, and youll be fine. Talk to Dr. Ayres, she is a great person (rare in Biochem).
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult and confusing quiz/exam questions. Instructions are unclear. Some of the TAs were completely incompetent. I had issues in a lab and she condescended me for hours while TAs "helped" only for her to realize that the equipment was broken. I learned nothing, I was in fight or flight the whole time. Completely shocked that I got an A

I like Dr. Ayres. She is caring and humorous. I agree with the other posts that her quizzes and worksheets are pretty tricky, but they are doable with the help of your classmates and TAs outside of the class. Minor mistakes in the manual, but not a big deal. Regardless of the grades you get, she gives the top 30% an A. You learn to think critically

Class structure for summer was 300pts from quizzes 300 from wkshts 400 from final. Wkshts are easy and asking questions is encouraged, they are really helpful for this lab Quizzes can be challenging, it was open notebook though same for final. Summer was about 6hrs of work a week (not counting lab time) (/2 for normal semester). A lot of writing
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class has a lot of homework and quizzes. Even more work if you are doing writing. But she offers a lot of help. If you go to her office hours, she explains everything with passion and care. Midterm and final exams are very challenging and require a lot of thinking. Overall, I think if you put enough work in, you would be fine.

I had a 73% & she had to curve the class so much that it was considered a B b/c its so hard. Have to rewrite entire manual before quizzes. I only passed 1/8 quizzes (weighted heavy). She is EXTREMELY rude & condescending. Whole class was confused & she just threatened to use it against us on the 40% of grade final instead of helping us understand.

This lab consists of worksheets, quizzes, lab performance, and a lab final. The quiz and final questions can be a little difficult and are worth a bulk of the points. However, Dr. Ayres and the TAs are super helpful with helping students both in the lab and outside the course. There are many office hours throughout the week and the final is curved.

She always tries her best to accommodate students and was always there throughout the course to help students out. She also gave extra tries on the worksheets and curved the lab final really hard to give all of us a chance at a good grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Ayres as a lab coordinator. She was very helpful with filling out the lab worksheets and there are so many TA office hours through the week as well.

Look, I gotta be honest: since this is a senior class, no one wanted to really be there, but we had to in order to graduate. Dr. Ayres is sarcastic and kinda rude during her couple of lectures. But, grading depends on the TA, so good luck there. You do get to use your notebook on quizzes and the final, but theres so much to write from the manual.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers
